The situation can no longer continue once the calendar passes 1450: it closes without a victor, and the modifiers, the sword rule and the organisation go with it. Nobody receives the victory rewards.

A bleak closing event exists for this case (The Dream Dies: −10 stability and Shattered Administration across the region for 50 years — maximum control −10%, fort defence −25%, unrest +0.5), but in the current build it is tied to a later date than the situation's own end and is not expected to appear. See Known issues.

docs.title: Flavour along the way
docs.text: A dozen flavour events colour the interregnum for Persianate courts — a ghazal-master in Shiraz looking for a patron, Mustawfī's Nuzhat al-Qulūb laid before the throne, Dilshad Khatun, the quarrel of yasa and sharīʿa, amirs demanding iqṭāʿ, the Dīwān's petition, a shaykh at court, a dervish in the bazaar, a widow's endowment, the mountain chiefs, a Türkmen migration, an Anatolian beg. They nudge the estates and the axis rather than decide the contest.

docs.title: Practical advice
docs.text:
• Read the opening event as a choice of mid-game, not of opening bonus. The regency pays +0.5 legitimacy a month and starts a clock; the farr costs you on day one and starts a trial by conquest; the ghazā is steady only while you have someone to fight; the governorate is safe and goes nowhere on its own.
  • Guard your province capitals. Under the sword rule a fallen provincial capital takes its whole province with it. A single lost siege can cost a dozen locations, and nothing is returned at the peace.
  • Do not hide behind walls. With −66% fort defence, forts buy days, not seasons. Meet the enemy in the field or lose the province.
  • Press Claim is free. A contender never needs to fabricate a casus belli against a neighbouring member.
  • Conquest is only half the price. What you take arrives conquered. Decide early whether you are a chancery realm (build Local Dīwāns, Consolidate) or an amirs' realm (Grant the Yurt), because each integration pushes the axis the same way — and the axis is a victory condition.
  • The Five Seats must be yours, not your vassal's. Plan to annex or take over any subject sitting on Tabriz, Baghdad, Soltaniyeh, Isfahan or Shiraz.
  • A Tāzīk victory runs through the Matter of Tork. A Türk victory does not have a matching requirement at present, which makes it the shorter road on paper.

See also: The Erānzamīn organisation, The Borrowed Mandate, The Ilkhanate Governorate, Farr — the Proof of Fortune, The Burden of the Sword, The Matter of Tork, Türk vs Tāzīk, Government reforms, Starting the game.

docs.title: Estate privileges
docs.text:
Every grant is a line in the register: something the state gains, something it agrees not to see.

This page is the complete list of the privileges the mod adds or changes, grouped by estate, with their conditions and effects as they stand in 1.4.

docs.title: What they represent
docs.text: A Persianate ruler governed less by statute than by grant: the iqṭāʿ assigned to a commander, the soyurghāl that made it hereditary and immune, the patent of tarkhan exemption, the charter confirming an endowment, the diploma investing a chief accountant or a chief of the merchants. Each was a bargain between the throne and a body of its servants, and each named an office or an institution with a long record: the Ṣāḥib-Dīwān, the Mustawfī al-Mamālik, the Amīr al-Umarāʾ, the Naqīb al-Ashrāf. The privilege panel is where those bargains are struck.

docs.title: How to read the tables
docs.text:
• Sat is the estate's target satisfaction; power is that estate's power. Both are percentages: "Sat +5%, power +50%".
  • Max tax is the ceiling on what an estate can be assessed. Many privileges lower the granting estate's own ceiling and raise someone else's; this is the quiet half of almost every bargain.
  • Urban / rural are maximum control in towns and cities and in the countryside.
  • Turk / Tazik, centralization and the like are monthly movement on the societal values; see Turk vs Tazik.
  • PI gain is the monthly gain of political influence (see the end of this page).
  • "PS only" means the privilege is offered only to a country with the Persianate Sultanate government.

Three patterns recur:

  • Rival pairs. Two privileges, one from each elite, that cannot be held together. You must lose the one to grant the other.
  • Crossing the line. Two privileges break the division of pen and sword set by the Persianate Bureaucracy reform: one lets the Dīwān command armies, the other seats amirs in the cabinet.
  • The Matter of Tork lock. Four privileges (marked ‡) cannot be granted while the Matter of Tork is open and unanswered unless the Amirs, the Dīwān and the Tribes are all at 50% satisfaction or better.

docs.title: Political influence
docs.text:
1.4 introduced political influence (PI) as a currency gained each month from the ruler and a full cabinet. The mod's rule of thumb is that political influence pays for acts inside the existing order and legitimacy pays for changing it.

Within the estates, that means:

Source Effect on monthly PI gain Mustawfī al-Mamālik +10% Mongol-Persian Documentary Synthesis +10% Qānūn Codification +10% Dīwān of the Realms (building) +10% Amīr al-Umarāʾ −10% Umarāʾ at the Dīwān −10% Ṣāḥib-Dīwān Plenipotentiary −15% (and −0.15 monthly legitimacy: the vizier is seen to rule)

A working chancery makes the court's orders move by register; a camp that has taken over the offices, or a minister who has taken over the throne's business, drains them.

The estate action that spends it is Summon the Amirs' Tümens: 15 political influence, or 5 when the Dīwān outweighs the Amirs (see the Amirs estate). The other places the mod prices in political influence (demanding fealty and integrating governorates, posting a darugha, enthroning a khan) belong to Custody of the Ulus, the Ilkhanate governorate, Hordes and Ulus Chaghatay.

docs.title: Practical notes
docs.text:
• Read the max-tax entries before the headline effects. Five chancery privileges later, the Dīwān may be nearly untaxable and the burghers and peasants carrying the difference; the amir list does the same for the Amirs, ending in Universal Tarkhan, which removes them from the tax base altogether.
  • Power is cumulative and large. A single +100% privilege on top of the demographic bases can tip an estate into its "powerful" effects, good and bad.
  • The two line-crossing privileges are the strongest single moves on the Turk vs Tazik value available from the panel, and each costs the other elite 10% satisfaction and 15% power.
  • The three waqf charters buy satisfaction and legitimacy cheaply, and each one surrenders the court's power to dissolve endowments.

See also: Dīwān estate, Amirs estate, The Maẓālim court, Turk vs Tazik, Matter of Tork, Buildings, Government reforms.

docs.title: The Farr Under Examination
docs.text:
Whose head does heaven crown?

Farr-i īzadī, the divine glory that rests on a rightful king, was by 1337 an ordinary part of Islamic political thought: Niẓām al-Mulk, Ghazālī and Naṣīr al-Dīn Ṭūsī all write of kingship as a trust from God, shown by justice and by fortune. What was unusual after the fall of the Ilkhans was to rest a throne on it alone — with no khan's edict and no caliph's diploma behind it. A house that does so has turned its legitimacy from a status into a claim, and a claim can be checked: by victory, by the state of the rains, by whether the mints and the pulpits take up the new name.

Adopting the Farr-i Īzadī government reform starts that check. The disaster is called The Farr Under Examination in game (its tooltips also call it the Farr Proof of Fortune). It begins as soon as the reform is adopted, cannot be avoided, and is the central content of the farr road. The reform is open only to members of the Erānzamīn organisation; see government reforms for what it gives by itself.

docs.title: The wager
docs.text:
On the day it begins you lose 50 legitimacy: by the logic of the old chancery, the edict that appointed you was the basis of your standing, and you have just disowned it. While the examination runs:

Effect Value What it stands for Monthly legitimacy −1.0 The claim consumes the credibility it asserts Minting income −40% The mints still strike the Ilkhan's name Amirs estate target satisfaction −10% The amīrs watch a king claim what a khan gave Clergy estate target satisfaction −5% The Friday sermon is not yet read for you Burghers estate target satisfaction −5% The bazaar distrusts the unnamed coin Court spending efficiency −10% Diplomatic reputation −1 Foreign chanceries omit the title

There is no separate score. Legitimacy is the ledger, and the panel shows three bars that read it: Months at Legitimacy ≥ 95 (Vindication) out of 60, Months at Legitimacy ≤ 40 (Lapse) out of 60, and Months Elapsed (Endurance, year 25) out of 300.

docs.title: The standing offset: war
docs.text: While the examination runs and you are at war with anyone, The Doctrine Tested in War gives +0.3 monthly legitimacy and +7.5% Amirs satisfaction. War slows the drain; it does not pay for it.

docs.title: Events on the field
docs.text:
Every one of these fires an event the first time; each event has an option to silence that kind of notice, or all of them, after which the effect is applied quietly.

Event Legitimacy Also A major battle won +1 A battle lost −2 A location gained +1 A location lost −3 A war won +5 Conquest in the Light of Heaven for 12 months: +0.4 monthly legitimacy, +0.05 monthly prestige. Each further victory extends it A war lost −10 Defeat in the Light of Heaven for 6 months: −1.0 monthly legitimacy, −0.10 monthly prestige, −5% Amirs satisfaction The capital lost −20 The Capital Lost: −2.0 monthly legitimacy and −0.20 monthly prestige. It stays until the examination ends

Victories are counted from major battles only, not skirmishes. Handing land to your own subject is not counted as a lost war.

docs.text:
Situation Net monthly legitimacy from the examination At peace −1.0 At war −0.7 At war, within a year of a won war −0.3 The same, with all four apparatus claimed +0.2 At peace, with all four apparatus claimed −0.5

Other sources of legitimacy in your realm stack on top of this, but the examination itself is never fully cancelled by the apparatus. The lump sums — battles, cities, wars won — do most of the lifting.

docs.title: The apparatus of sovereignty
docs.text:
Four buttons on the panel, each available once legitimacy reaches a threshold. None is automatic. Each costs legitimacy on the spot and gives two modifiers: a refund, which cancels part of the examination's penalty for as long as it runs, and a legacy, which outlasts it. Each can be claimed once, in any order.

Button Needs Costs Refund (while the examination runs) Legacy Strike the Sikka 50 −10 The Sikka Cuts Your Name: +40% minting income, +5% Burghers, +0.1 monthly legitimacy The Dār al-Ḍarb of Our House, 25 years: +5% tax efficiency, +5% Dīwān satisfaction Claim the Khutba 65 −15 The Khutba Reads Your Name: +5% Clergy, +0.1 monthly legitimacy The Khutba Precedent, 25 years: +5% Clergy, +1 tolerance of the true faith Proclaim the Royal Hunt and Nawrūz Court 80 −20 The Amīrs Bow at the Hunt: +10% Amirs, +0.1 monthly legitimacy The Hunt and the Nawrūz Court, 25 years: +15% Tribes, +5% Amirs, lower Amirs and Tribes rebel growth Assume the Title of Pādishāh 90 −25 The Title Brought Into Line: +0.2 monthly legitimacy Pādishāh-i Īrān, permanent: −15% antagonism received, +1 diplomatic reputation, +0.05 monthly prestige. The realm becomes a kingdom and gains 25 prestige

Coin and sermon were the two public signs of sovereignty in the Islamic world; the hunt and the Nawrūz audience are how a Persianate king is seen to be one by the men of the sword; the title completes the claim.

Two of the claims make enemies inside Erānzamīn:

  • Strike the Sikka: every member that rules as a Chinggisid Regency takes the opinion penalty "Ignored the Hallowed bloodline of Genghis Khan" (−150, fading by 1 a year) and gains the Succession of Erānzamīn casus belli on you.
  • Claim the Khutba: every member that rules as a Ghāzī Sultanate takes "Read khutbah in his own name" (−100, fading by 2 a year) and gains the same casus belli.

docs.text:
These happen to the king, once each, the first time legitimacy falls to the mark.

docs.title: Omens
docs.text:
A just king's reign is supposed to show in the world, so the world is read. In most years one or more omens arrive; each kind has a two-year pause before it can return. Most offer a public reading, which gambles, or a cautious one.

Omen The stakes A Comet Stands Above the Throne Publish the reading: 60% +6, 40% −8. Keep it at court: ±2 The Earth Itself Has Spoken Ride to the ruins (4.5 months' income): 65% +5, 35% −3. Leave it to the ʿulamāʾ: Clergy −3%, +1 or −3 Plague in the Realm Lead the prayers: +4 or −10 at even odds. Open the granaries (nine months' income): 70% +3, 30% −4. Withdraw to the citadel: −6, Burghers −8% The Rains Are Withheld Remit the land tax (six months' income; Peasants +5%): 70% +4, 30% −2. Blame the assessors (Dīwān −8%): 45% +2, 55% −4 The Rains Are Generous Let the sermon say it: +4. Tax the surplus: gain three months' income, +1 The Stars Incline Strike the conjunction on the coins: +15. File the tables: +5 for a small fee The King Takes the Lion Parade the skin: 65% +4, 35% −3. Feast the amīrs: +2 legitimacy, +5 prestige for a small fee The Homay Lands on the King's Shoulder +50 legitimacy. Once ever, and vanishingly rare

Plague is three times as likely between 1346 and 1350. Drought and good rains never fall in the same year.

docs.title: The four endings
docs.text: Checked every month, in this order.

docs.title: Broken — The Amīrs Have Taken the Throne
docs.text:
When: legitimacy reaches 0.

The ruler is killed. A Borjigin amīr of Persianized Mongol culture takes the throne, the Farr-i Īzadī reform is replaced by the Amīr Sultanate, and all four legacies are stripped. The realm gains 25 legitimacy under its new master, Amirs +25% and Tribes +20% satisfaction, Dīwān −20% and Burghers −10%, and carries An Unproved Boast for 25 years (−0.10 monthly prestige, −1 diplomatic reputation, +10% antagonism received). While that modifier lasts the reform cannot be taken again.

docs.title: Vindicated — Farr Manifest
docs.text:
When: 60 months, not necessarily consecutive, at legitimacy 95 or higher.

+20 legitimacy, +50 prestige, +10 stability. Farr-i Īzadī is replaced at once by the Age of Renaissance reform Iranian Kingship, and Farr Manifest applies for ten years: +0.1 monthly legitimacy, +10% Amirs and +5% Tribes satisfaction, lower rebel growth for both, −20% antagonism received, +1 diplomatic reputation. The legacies stay.

docs.title: Lapsed — The Doctrine Has Lapsed
docs.text:
When: 60 months, not necessarily consecutive, at legitimacy 40 or lower.

No coup; the court simply stops using the formula. −15 legitimacy, −25 prestige, the reform is removed, and An Unproved Boast becomes permanent. The house cannot declare the farr again. Legacies already earned run out their terms.

docs.title: Endured — The Claim Stands
docs.text:
When: 300 months have passed and nothing above has happened.

+10 legitimacy, +15 prestige. The reform is replaced by Iranian Kingship, and Farr Endured is permanent: +0.10 monthly legitimacy and −10% antagonism received.

Abandoning the reform by other means also ends the examination, with nothing gained.

Either Vindicated or Endured settles the question of right for forming Persia; the broken outcomes do not.

docs.title: How to manage it
docs.text:
The examination opens by taking 50 legitimacy, which puts most houses at or under 40 on the first day — and every month at 40 or less counts toward the Lapse. You have five years of such months in total, over the whole run, before the doctrine dies quietly. The first task is therefore to climb out of that zone and stay out.

  1. Be at war when you adopt the reform, or immediately after. At peace you lose 12 legitimacy a year from the examination alone.
  2. Win wars, not just battles. A won war is +5 and a year of +0.4 a month; keep one victory inside every twelve months and the modifier never drops.
  3. Take Strike the Sikka early. It costs 10, returns 0.1 a month, restores your minting income, and its threshold is the lowest. Do not claim it while it would drop you back to 40 or below — and remember it hands every regent in Erānzamīn a casus belli.
  4. Space the later claims. Each costs more than the last, and the costs cascade: claiming all four at their thresholds spends 70 legitimacy. Claim from above the threshold, in a year when a victory is paying.
  5. Decide which ending you are playing for. Vindication needs five years at 95 or more, and Pādishāh alone costs 25, so take the title first and climb afterwards. If you cannot hold 95, a realm that stays above 40 and keeps its capital reaches Endured in year 25 and receives the same Iranian Kingship.
  6. Guard the capital above everything. Its loss costs 20 at once and 2.0 a month for the rest of the examination; taking the city back does not lift it.
  7. Use the omens as a bank. The cautious options are small but safe; the gambles are worth taking when you are far from both 40 and 95.

See also: government reforms, the Persianate sultanate, the Erānzamīn situation, the Erānzamīn organisation, Türk vs Tāzīk, the Burden of the Sword (the parallel examination on the ghāzī road), the Matter of Tork (what comes after), known issues.

docs.title: The Burden of the Sword
docs.text:
Heaven's reward attends the holy warrior — the umma is checking.

The ghāzī title was the most widely understood claim a Muslim ruler could make in the fourteenth century: the frontier warrior who defends and extends the lands of Islam, recognised by the jurists and, where possible, by a diploma from the Abbasid caliph kept at Cairo. The Muẓaffarid Mubāriz al-Dīn Muḥammad built his rule on it — the caliph's name in the sermon, the censor in the bazaar of Shīrāz — and showed its weakness too, for a ghāzī with no ghazā to fight is a title and nothing more. Preachers, volunteers and jurists all keep count of which wars were fought, and against whom.

Adopting the Ghāzī Sultanate government reform starts that count. The disaster is The Burden of the Sword. It begins as soon as the reform is adopted and cannot be avoided. Where the Farr Under Examination is paid in victory of any kind, the Burden is paid in war against the right kind of enemy, and it decays at rest.

docs.title: The hunger
docs.text:
On the day it begins you lose 60 legitimacy. While it runs:

Effect Value What it stands for Monthly legitimacy −0.5 The claim, unpaid Clergy estate target satisfaction −5% The jurists withhold endorsement Levy size −10% The volunteers do not come to a quiet court Monthly religious influence −0.10 The pulpits cool Monthly prestige −0.05 Foreign chanceries omit the title

Legitimacy is the ledger. The panel shows five bars: Sword of Islam (months at legitimacy ≥ 75) out of 60, Wars won against dar al-harb out of 2, Lapse / Rising (months at legitimacy ≤ 25) out of 60, Frontier expectations failed out of 2, and Endurance (total disaster months) out of 300.

docs.title: War as the standing offset
docs.text:
A realm that holds the Ghāzī Sultanate reform (or its successor, Sword of The Sharia) gains a bonus for every month it is at war with a qualifying enemy. These work in and out of the disaster.

At war with Monthly legitimacy Monthly prestige Levy size Manpower A country of a different religion — Fighting against Infidels, Heretics or Corruption on Earth +0.75 +0.10 +25% +25% A country that keeps Mongol law — Fighting Against Muslims who Cling to Primitive Law +0.50 +0.05 +12.5% +12.5% A country under Lax Enforcement of the ḥisba — Fighting Against Muslims who Tolerate Corruption +0.25 +0.025 +12.5% +12.5%

Each is judged separately, so a war against an enemy that fits more than one description earns more than one. Against the −0.5 of the Burden, a war with a realm of another religion nets +0.25 a month; peace nets the full −0.5. The reform itself adds a further +0.1 at all times.

The house must also be in order. A ghāzī court that itself keeps Mongol law, or itself runs Lax Enforcement, is designed to pay a standing penalty to legitimacy, prestige, levies and manpower. Repeal the yāsā before you take the reform.

docs.title: What the field pays
docs.text:
As with the farr, each of these first appears as an event with options to silence that kind of notice. Battles and wars against rebels do not count.

Event Legitimacy Also A battle won +1, and +2 more if the enemy is non-Muslim A battle lost −2 A location gained +1 A location taken from a non-Muslim realm +6 in all +10 prestige (A Mosque on Conquered Ground) A location lost −3 A war won +1.5, plus the credit below A war lost −3 The Sword Failed in the Field for 6 months: −1.0 monthly legitimacy, −5% morale The capital lost −25 The Seat of the Ghazi Fallen: −0.3 monthly legitimacy, −0.1 monthly prestige until the Burden ends; it also bars the Guardian ending

docs.title: Which wars are credited
docs.text:
When a war is won, the defeated enemy is classed:

The defeated realm Credit Non-Muslim — the dār al-ḥarb +10 legitimacy; counts toward the two wars the Sword of Islam needs; The Banner Carried Forward for 12 months (+0.4 monthly legitimacy, +5% morale); resets the frontier expectation Muslim in name, with the scholar's ruling in hand +5 legitimacy; six months of The Banner Carried Forward Muslim in name, without the ruling +2 legitimacy, and A Fatwa Arrives Questioning Your Wars An ordinary Sunni realm Nothing, and the same fatwa

"Muslim in name" means a Muslim realm ruling as a Chinggisid Regency, or one whose rite is neither Sunni nor Shia. A Shia realm that is not a regency earns neither credit nor complaint. The fatwa asks you to pay the scholars (six months' income; Clergy +5%) or stand by the war (−8 legitimacy, Clergy −10%); it cannot return within two years.

The scholar's ruling comes by event, not by a button. From time to time The Scholar Proposes a Ruling: that a Muslim prince who governs by the yāsā has not entered the law. Endorse it (+5 legitimacy, Clergy −5%) or pay for it (twelve months' income, +5 legitimacy) and you hold the ruling for good; refuse (Clergy +5%) and the offer may return after two years.

The panel also carries Ask Ulemma for a Jihad Ruling., usable every six months while you hold the Ghāzī Sultanate reform: choose a neighbour and gain the Ghozva Holy War casus belli on it. The casus belli is for realms outside the Muslim religions; once you hold the scholar's ruling it is designed to extend to Muslim realms that keep Mongol law.

docs.title: The apparatus of the ghāzī
docs.text:
Four buttons, each claimed once. Each costs legitimacy and gives a refund, which cancels part of the Burden while it runs, and a permanent legacy. With all four refunds standing every line of the Burden's penalty is cancelled.

Button Needs Costs Refund (while the Burden runs) Legacy (permanent) Establish the Hisba Legitimacy 50 −10 The Censor's House Cleaning: +0.1 monthly legitimacy, +5% Clergy The Hisba Apparatus: +0.05 monthly religious influence, +1 tolerance of the true faith, +3% Clergy Endow the Frontier Lodges Legitimacy 60 and six months' income in the treasury −15 and six months' income The Lodges of the Frontier: +0.1 monthly legitimacy, +10% levy size The Lodges Stand: +3% levy size, +5% manpower, +5% Tribes Seek the Caliph's Diploma Legitimacy 60 −15 The Caliph's Diploma: +0.1 monthly legitimacy, +0.10 monthly religious influence The Diploma Exists: +1 diplomatic reputation, +0.05 monthly prestige, +5% Clergy. Also +30 prestige Assume the Style of Sultan of the Ghazis Legitimacy 90, or 75 with the diploma −25 Sultan of the Ghazis: +0.2 monthly legitimacy, +0.05 monthly prestige The Title in the Protocol: +0.10 monthly prestige, −15% antagonism received, +1 diplomatic reputation. The realm becomes a kingdom and gains 50 prestige

There are two ladders to the title: through Cairo, at 75, as Mubāriz al-Dīn climbed it; or without Cairo, at 90, in the house's own name.

docs.title: The designated frontier
docs.text:
Endowing the lodges gathers the volunteers, and the same day The Volunteers Are Gathered — Where? asks where to point them:

  • The Caucasus Gate — Georgia, Derbent, the steppe;
  • The Road to Rum — Anatolia, Trebizond, what is left of Constantinople;
  • The Ghaznavid Road — Hindustan;
  • or send them home (−5 legitimacy, Tribes −5%).

A designated frontier gives +10% manpower and +5% levy size while the Burden runs. It is also a promise. If 60 months pass without a war won against a non-Muslim realm, The Volunteers Came for War fires: a frontier expectation is marked as failed, you lose 2 to 5 legitimacy and some Tribes satisfaction, and The Volunteers Disbanded applies for three years (−0.2 monthly legitimacy, −5% levy size). The count then starts again. As scripted, any war won against a non-Muslim realm keeps the promise, wherever it is fought.

Two failed expectations are one of the conditions of the Dervish Rising.

docs.title: Internal campaigns
docs.text:
The fifth button, Launch an Internal Campaign, turns the censor's apparatus on the realm itself. It needs:

  • The Hisba Apparatus (from Establish the Hisba);
  • the ḥisba law set to Strict Enforcement or The Muhtasib-King;
  • at least one Ḥisba Office building;
  • fewer than three campaigns so far.

Each launch costs three months' income and 3 legitimacy, then offers a target:

Campaign Lasting mark (5 years) At once Close the taverns — The Taverns Sealed Burghers −5%, −2.5% tax efficiency, a little prosperity lost Burghers −10% Disperse the suspect shaykhs — The Shaykhs Dispersed −1 tolerance of heretics, +0.05 monthly religious influence, Peasants −3% Clergy +5% Move on the other branch — The Other Branch Quieted +10% conversion speed, −1 tolerance of heretics, +0.05 monthly religious influence Unrest in one location

The credit shrinks each time: +5 legitimacy and +8% Clergy for the first, +3 and +5% for the second, +1 and +3% for the third. Net of the launch cost that is +2, 0 and −2 legitimacy. The first campaign reads as righteousness; the third as theatre.

docs.title: The ḥisba law
docs.text:
Hisba — Enforcement of Public Morals is a religious law open to every Muslim realm, with or without the disaster. It sets how hard the muḥtasib, the market censor, walks the bazaar: piety mobilised into levies, or left to the merchants.

Policy Available to Effects Lax Enforcement — The Open Bazaar All Burghers pleased, Clergy displeased; +2.5% tax efficiency, +5% cabinet efficiency, a little prosperity; −10% levy size, −10% morale, −0.05 monthly religious influence; drifts toward Mysticism. Makes you a credited target for ghāzī neighbours Customary Enforcement — The Qāḍī's Discretion All +2.5% satisfaction for every estate; beer and liquor imports banned Strict Enforcement — The Stick in the Bazaar All Clergy pleased; +10% levy size, +25% morale, +0.05 monthly religious influence; Burghers −5%, −2.5% tax efficiency; wine, beer and liquor imports banned; drifts toward Jurisprudence The Muhtasib-King Ghāzī Sultanate or Sword of The Sharia; never after the murīd bond Clergy +10%; +25% levy size, +25% morale, +0.10 monthly religious influence, +25% conversion speed; Burghers −10%, −5% tax efficiency, prosperity lost; the same import bans Ẓill Allāh — The Shadow of God Shia realms at Mysticism −50, or any realm that has sworn the murīd bond +0.1 monthly legitimacy, +0.1 monthly religious influence, +25% morale, +10% levy size, Burghers +5%, +2.5% tax efficiency, +1 tolerance of heretics; Clergy −5%

The last two are the two poles of the mod's religious politics: enforcement as the throne's own identity, and authority resting in the person of the guide. Swearing the murīd bond in the Matter of Tork closes the first for good and opens the second.

The Ḥisba Office is a one-level building for towns and cities, open to any Muslim realm: +5% local maximum control, +5% local conversion speed, more Clergy power and some Burghers unrest.

docs.title: Signs and omens
docs.text:
Three events fire once each as legitimacy falls: The Preacher Cools at 35, The Friday Khutba Turns Colder at 20, and Bī-Ghazā — "without ghazā" — at 10. Each lets you buy some warmth back with gold or endure it.

Other events arrive at random, each at most once in two years:

Event The choice A Famous Preacher's Sermon Turns Patronise him (three months' income; 60% +4, 40% −3) or ignore him (40% +1, 60% −4) The Volunteers Drift Recall them (4.5 months' income, −2) or let them go (−5, Tribes −5%) News of Infidel Victory Answer the call (+3) or look away (−5) The Muhtasib Turns on the Court — only with The Hisba Apparatus, at legitimacy 35 or less Submit to the audit (Clergy +10%, −15 prestige, −2) or curb him (Clergy −10%, −5) The Returned Ghazi Honour him (three months' income; +3, Tribes +5%) or a small purse (−4, Tribes −5%) The Neglected Ribat Rebuild it (six months' income; +2, Clergy +5%) or mourn (−6, Clergy −5%) The Banners Flock Feast and enrol them (1.5 months' income; +4, Tribes +5%) or bless them (+1) The Captives Return Pay the balance (three months' income; +5, Clergy +5%) or let the families finish (+1)

docs.title: The four endings
docs.text: Checked every month, in this order.

docs.title: Sword of Islam
docs.text:
When: legitimacy at 75 or more, 60 months (not necessarily consecutive) spent at 75 or more, and two wars won against non-Muslim realms.

+25 legitimacy, +50 prestige, +10 stability. The Ghāzī Sultanate reform is replaced by Sword of The Sharia, and Sword of Islam is permanent: +0.2 monthly legitimacy, +10% levy size, +10% manpower, +10% morale, +2 tolerance of the true faith, +0.10 monthly prestige. The legacies stay.

docs.title: The Dervish Rising
docs.text:
When: legitimacy at 25 or less, 60 months spent at 25 or less, The Lodges Stand held, and two frontier expectations failed.

The volunteers you housed follow a shaykh instead. The ruler is killed and replaced by a Shia man of the lodges; the country becomes Shia; the reform is replaced by Mushaʿshaʿ Messianism; all four legacies are stripped; −25 legitimacy, Clergy −15%, Tribes −20%; and After the Rising lasts 25 years (−0.10 monthly legitimacy, −2 tolerance of heretics, Clergy −10%, −0.10 monthly religious influence). The realm survives as something else: this is the mod's picture of how a frontier devotion becomes a messianic movement.

docs.title: Guardian of the Thughur
docs.text:
When: 300 months have passed, the realm borders a non-Muslim country, and the capital has not been lost during the Burden.

+12 legitimacy, +20 prestige. The reform is replaced by Sword of The Sharia, and Guardian of the Thughur is permanent: +0.1 monthly legitimacy, +5% levy size, +5% morale, +0.05 monthly prestige. This is the murābiṭ's answer — holding the wall is service too — and an interior realm cannot give it.

docs.title: The Doctrine Lapses
docs.text:
When: 60 months spent at legitimacy 25 or less, without the conditions of the Rising.

−15 legitimacy, −25 prestige. The reform is removed and cannot be taken again, The Muhtasib-King goes with it, and The Doctrine Furniture is permanent: −0.10 monthly prestige, −0.05 monthly legitimacy, Clergy −5%. The legacies remain.

Sword of Islam and Guardian of the Thughur both settle the question of right for forming Persia. For what Sword of The Sharia gives, see government reforms.

docs.title: After the Burden: the lodge and the volunteers
docs.text: Sword of The Sharia opens the Mutaṭawwiʿa Lodge, a one-level building for any settlement, staffed by clergy: it raises local manpower, garrison size (+12.5%) and local Clergy power. Where a lodge stands, the levy Call the Ghazis raises Ghazi Volunteers from the clergy pops: light cavalry that deals 20% more morale damage and takes 20% less, but takes 20% more casualties and deals 10% fewer, with +1 initiative and a lighter supply train. They fight best in sparse country, on flat land and in desert, and badly in forest and wetlands.

docs.title: How to manage it
docs.text:
1. Choose the reform only with an enemy in reach. You need a country of another religion to be at war with for most of the next decades, and two won wars against non-Muslims for the best ending. A Muslim neighbour of another rite sustains the monthly offset but does not count toward the Sword.
  2. Open with a war. You start 60 down and lose six a year at peace; at war with a realm of another faith you gain three a year, plus everything the field pays. Locations taken from non-Muslim realms are the richest single source in the whole disaster.
  3. Establish the Hisba at 50, then the diploma and the lodges at 60. The diploma lowers the title's threshold from 90 to 75. The lodges cost six months' income and commit you to a frontier.
  4. Endow the lodges only if you mean to fight. Without The Lodges Stand the Dervish Rising cannot happen, and failure falls back to the quieter Lapse — at the price of leaving the −10% levy penalty standing.
  5. Mind the two clocks. Five years in total at 25 or below ends the doctrine. Five years in total at 75 or above, with two wars won, wins it. Claims cost legitimacy, so take them when a victory is paying.
  6. Check the border before year 25. The Guardian ending needs a non-Muslim neighbour. An interior realm that has neither won nor lapsed simply stays under the Burden until it wins, lapses or finds a frontier.
  7. Keep internal campaigns for a bad year. Only the first is worth its cost, and it requires the strict side of the ḥisba law, with what that does to your burghers.

See also: government reforms, the Persianate sultanate, the Erānzamīn situation, buildings, the military system, ṭarīqa orders, the Farr Under Examination (the parallel examination on the farr road), the Matter of Tork (what comes after), known issues.

docs.title: Government reforms
docs.text:
In whose name is the khuṭba read and the sikka struck?

New in 1.4 — not yet verified in play

The four chancery "dresses" outside Iran (Mamluk, Delhi, Rasulid, Timurid) and the Age of Discovery reforms are in the files as described here but have not yet been checked through a full campaign.

This page is the complete list of the government reforms the mod adds or rewrites, with the name each carries in game. Reforms of the Persianate Sultanate are given in full; reforms that belong to another government or another system are listed by name at the end with a link to their own page.

docs.title: What the tree represents
docs.text: When Abū Saʿīd died without an heir in 1335 the Ilkhanate lost the one thing its successor states could not manufacture: a khan of Hülegü's line. Every amir, governor and dynasty on the plateau then had to answer the same question — by what right do you rule? — and the answers available were all orthodox Islamic political positions of the day: rule as deputy of a Chinggisid, rule as the Caliph's sword on the frontier, rule as a just king bearing the farr-i īzadī that the mirrors-for-princes had long since made part of Islamic kingship, rule by the army's assent, or decline to answer and administer. The Age of Traditions reforms are those answers. The later ages follow what the answers became: the Timurid settlement, the Türkmen confederations, and the Safavid fusion and its disciplining.

docs.title: How to read the tables
docs.text:
• Enact is how long the reform takes once chosen. "Event" means the reform cannot be taken or dropped from the reform panel at all; it is granted and removed by events.
  • Percentages on estates are satisfaction equilibrium ("satisfaction") and estate power ("power").
  • Türk and Tāzīk are monthly pushes on the Türk vs Tāzīk slider; centralization pushes work the same way on the base slider.
  • Shut out by lists the reforms you must not hold. Exclusions are mutual unless noted.

docs.title: The chassis
docs.text:
Every Persianate Sultanate runs on one of five versions of the same chancery. They are mutually exclusive, cannot be chosen from the panel, and are what makes the Dīwān and Amirs estates, the tribal levy system and the iqṭāʿ buildings work.

Reform Who has it Effects Persianate Bureaucracy Every Iranian-world sultanate at start; granted to any new state the mod converts (see Persianate Sultanate) +10% cabinet efficiency, +10% tax efficiency, +0.10 centralization. Dīwān +25% power, +5% satisfaction, may sit in the cabinet. Amirs, nobles, burghers and clergy may not sit in the cabinet. Only Amirs may lead armies. Nobles −90% power. Levies: peasants −90%, Dīwān −90%, Amirs +30%, tribes +10%. +15% max urban control, +5% max rural control, +10% max estate tax, +2 cultural capacity, tributaries allowed. Mamluk Government Mamluks (MAM) The base Mamluk mechanics (promotion, Mamluk barracks, +0.1 monthly army tradition, −10% court spending efficiency) on the same chancery: +5% cabinet efficiency, +5% tax efficiency, Dīwān +15% power. Levies: peasants −100%, burghers −50%, Dīwān −90%, Amirs +75%, tribes +10%. +10% land morale. +15% max urban and +10% max rural control. Same cabinet and command rules as the Iranian form. The Delhi Dispensation Delhi (DLH) and the Muslim Indian minors at start; the Delhi breakaway sultanates when they appear. Muslim, capital in South Asia. +10% cabinet efficiency, +10% tax efficiency, +15% max estate tax, +0.15 centralization. Dīwān +25% power. Nobles −60% power (the Hindu landed nobility remains a real estate). Levies: peasants −50%, Dīwān −90%, Amirs +40%, tribes +10%. Can build Mamluk barracks. +15% max urban control. Rasulid Chancery Rasulid Yemen (YEM); a Zaydi imam who turns sultan +5% cabinet efficiency, +5% tax efficiency, Dīwān +15% power. Levies: peasants −50%, burghers −25%, Amirs +75%, tribes +25%. Tribes +75% power. +10% land morale. +20% max urban control, −5% max rural control. Timurid Empire The Ṣāḥib-qirān's realm (TIM), when it settles down through the Rise of Timur situation The Persianate Bureaucracy block with heavier horse (Amirs levy +40%, tribes +20%), +3 cultural capacity, +1 reform slot, +50% loot, −20% antagonism received. Needs no separate answer to the legitimacy question.

docs.text:
A Persianate Sultanate that holds none of these (and none of the non-Iranian chassis or the special reforms that count as an answer) suffers Unsettled Legitimacy: −0.6 legitimacy a month, Amirs and Dīwān −20% satisfaction, clergy and burghers −15%. The opening event of the Erānzamīn situation, Hulagu's Seat Stands Empty, offers the choice; the reforms below are mutually exclusive.

Event Starts the Ghāzī Burden of the Sword. +0.1 legitimacy, +0.05 prestige a month. +10% manpower, +5% land morale, +15% army tradition from battles. Amirs +10% satisfaction, +25% power, +20% levy, and Amirs may sit in the cabinet. Two points the tooltips do not make obvious:

  • Amīr Sultanate does not, by itself, lift Unsettled Legitimacy as the files stand; only the released tributary marches are exempt. A self-made Amīr Sultanate nets about −0.45 legitimacy a month until it moves on. This looks unintended and is listed under known issues.
  • Farr-i Īzadī and Ghāzī Sultanate are wagers, not settlements. Each is replaced by its Age of Renaissance successor when its disaster ends well, and stripped when it ends badly.

docs.title: Roads through the tree
docs.text:
These are sketches, not rails.

  • The Timurid road. Chinggisid Regency → The Gurkani Regime → Timurid Synthesis with Ṣāḥib-Qirān → Sunnī Orthodoxy, Ṣadr Judiciary, Ghulām Corps. The realm never claims a crown of its own and never needs to.
  • The Persian-kingship road. Farr-i Īzadī → survive the Proof → Iranian Kingship with Circle of Justice → Khāṣṣa Crown Demesne, Ṣadr Judiciary, Tofangchī and Topchī Corps. The strongest Tāzīk drift in the tree; expect the Matter of Tork on the way.
  • The frontier road. Ghāzī Sultanate → win or hold the Burden → Sword of The Sharia → Sunnī Orthodoxy and either cavalry or ghulām.
  • The Türkmen road. Chinggisid Regency or Amīr Sultanate → Türkmen Confederation → (if Shia) Qizilbāsh Aristocracy, Murshid-i Kāmil, Soyurghal Grants.
  • The Safavid road. Any Türk-leaning start → Mushaʿshaʿ Messianism → Murshid-i Kāmil, Qizilbāsh Aristocracy, Imāmī Tashayyuʿ — and later, if the shāh wants his throne back from his own disciples, Ghulām Corps is closed to him for as long as the Qizilbāsh hold theirs.
  • The governor's road. Ilkhanate Governorate, fealty to a steward, and patience. See Ilkhanate Governorate.
